behaviour.text: Födan består främst av insekter, särskilt fjärilslarver och andra larver, som den söker på marken och i lägre grenar.

Honan ruvar ensam fem till sju ägg i 12 till 14 dagar, och båda föräldrarna matar ungarna.

lead.text: The Sombre Tit is a tit that favours macchia with scattered trees and bushes, including olive groves, plum orchards and other fruit trees.
It is also seen in open park-like country, especially in mountainous limestone terrain.

fieldMarks.text: Very large black bib that leaves the white cheek as only a narrow wedge
Brown-tinged greyish black cap reaching far down the head
Male sooty brownish black on crown and nape, female more chocolate brown there
Size and proportions of a Great Tit, with a fairly strong bill

voice.text: The simple song resembles a Marsh Tit's but with an impure voice, roughly "tjriv-tjriv-tjriv".
Calls are Blue Tit-like and scolding like a sparrow, sometimes with a harsher tone.
A characteristic call is a buzzing "tschrrrr", and the alarm is a fairly deep, Great Tit-like "tchetchetche".

whereWhen.text: The Sombre Tit does not occur in Sweden, and there are no reports in Artportalen from 2016 to 2025.
It is resident but may move to lower areas in parts of its range.
It occurs from sea level up to 2 300 metres.

behaviour.text: It feeds mainly on insects, especially caterpillars and other larvae, searching on the ground and in lower branches.
Compared with other tits it is fairly quiet and retiring.
It breeds from March to early August in holes in rotting fruit trees, in nest boxes or in rock crevices.
The female alone incubates five to seven eggs for 12 to 14 days, and both parents feed the young.

text.text: The Willow Tit is similar in colour, but the Sombre Tit has a larger black bib, a cap reaching further down the head and often a peaked crown.
Compared with the Marsh Tit, the Sombre Tit has a proportionally longer tail.
The Siberian Tit is a similar species but differs from the Sombre Tit in the colours of its plumage.
